description: Returns additions, amendments and removals between official sanctions list snapshots: US Treasury OFAC SDN and Consolidated, UK HM Treasury/FCDO, EU Financial Sanctions Files, Canada and Australia (new Canada/Australia coverage is entity-only). Use it to monitor what changed since a date; use sanctions_search_entries when you have a name, and sanctions_get_entry when you already know a list and id. Inputs (all optional, they narrow together): since (YYYY-MM-DD, default 7 days ago), list, change (added/amended/removed), limit (1 to 50, default 20) and cursor (next_cursor from the previous page, same filters). Output: changes[] with entry, changed fields, observed_at and proof (official file URL, SHA-256, source date), plus lists[] check times and next_cursor for paging or polling; lists are checked about every 6 hours. This is a monitoring feed, not a clearance decision: no change means none observed, the UN list is not covered, and the official publications are authoritative. Terms: read-only; MCP calls are never charged. Without a key, metered routes give 10 successful answers a day free (unmetered routes are unlimited); errors do not count. On the paid HTTP routes, errors and empty answers are free. An optional API key keeps its prepaid-credit policy. When the free answers run out, the error names the HTTP alternative.

change.description: One kind of change only Allowed: added, amended, removed; e.g. added.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from this tool's prior answer; s followed by 1 to 12 digits, e.g. s0. Keep filters unchanged; omit on first call.

list.description: One list only Allowed: ofac-sdn, ofac-consolidated, uk, eu, ca, au; e.g. ofac-sdn.

since.description: Changes observed on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD (default: 7 days ago); e.g. 2026-10-01. Must be a parseable YYYY-MM-DD date.
